text: Started incident audit across three hosts; preserving operations while investigating.
Auditing database access, billing, backups and authentication.
Auditing CI deployments, keys and archive ingress.
Initial review: internet SSH password scans and Grafana traversal probes not by themselves access; investigating successful sessions and writable upload paths.
Distinct-source audit found deploy accepted from 54.36.199.108, not CI or Maria; investigating unauthorized access and secret exposure.
54.36.199.108 deploy logins are brief recurring checks across many days, likely documented old monitoring box (vault deploy password). Not treating as intruder without corroboration.
Blocked execution of any PHP-like uploads and assets-cache paths at nginx; site home still 200.
Protected plaintext billing/shop dumps: root-only directory, existing files 0600, future dump umask 077; encrypted copies still transfer.
Removed credential disclosure and online password oracle hidden in rental-quote.php while retaining public quote operation. Original kept root-only for investigation.
Rotated compromised app database password (WordPress and MariaDB), updated report.cnf copy; validated report, orders, homepage.
Discovered unlisted jpark account in sudo group on web; investigating usage before disabling legacy access.
Revoked dormant contractor jpark: absent from staff directory, no successful logins in restored 14-day logs, internet password probes; removed sudo and locked login.
Restricted Git repo config holding GitHub token to root/developers; deploy can still read repo for 3-minute release.
Restricted MariaDB listener to office interface 10.20.0.20, preserving local Unix socket jobs; verifying website separately.
Removed unrestricted root rsync sudo grant for deploy, unused by release and a route to arbitrary root file modification; retained release and restart grants.
Replayed original hidden ref branch offline (response length only, no credential output); verifies 247-byte signature of logged attacker response.
Removed unlisted former contractor jpark WordPress administrator account (no authored posts); server password already locked and sudo removed.

Reassessment: original hidden-ref response offline ~244 bytes with NEW 24-char DB secret; old DB secret was 16 chars (report.cnf), so would have been ~236, not observed 247 from 172.56.216.189. That POST alone does not establish credential theft; long bike input can also produce 247. Rotated proactively. Continue monitoring for corroboration.

Resolved 11-byte mismatch: nginx log bytes include HTTP chunk framing; local normal curl 117 payload logged 128. Original hidden ref with old 16-char password produced 236 payload + 11 framing = 247, exactly the two remote 247 responses (70.120.249.96 Oct30; 172.56.216.189 Nov12). Thus both read DB credentials. Repeated later short quotes are ordinary. Report updated.
Mid-shift follow-up: checking for reattempts and cron regressions after credential rotation and remediation.
DB follow-up: recent dumps, SQL grants and listener checks.
CI follow-up: expected backup ingress, maintenance, 3-minute releases, no suspicious SSH.
Locked unlisted dormant jpark login on ci-01 as on web-01; no keys or successful restored-log logins; db-01 has no such account.
Considering safe quote source in CI so routine releases cannot restore prior secret-disclosing plugin branch.
Committed sanitized quote endpoint into CI canonical repo; the 3-minute release will keep it safe.
Verified secured quote persisted in next automated release and maintenance stays healthy.
Moved MariaDB secure_file_priv away from plaintext dump directory to isolated empty mysql-files directory; SQL FILE access cannot reach DB archives even if mistakenly granted.
Removed temporary CI worktree after canonical security commit; automated release remains healthy.
Continuing watch after next release and payout cycles; checking active sessions and customer paths.
Checking 16:57 settlement batch and db dump cycle without touching payment key.
CI follow-up after secure quote deployment: release and maintenance passing, backups and credentials restricted.
Nginx now denies direct access to wp-config.php and backup/editor copies from any IP; regular shop pages still 200.
Second db follow-up: payout batch, dump handoff, listener and secure_file_priv remain stable.
Late-shift web check at 17:00: current HTTP, blocked config, billing job, staff logins and repeat attempts.
17:00 db dump encrypted, root-only; unchanged app grant, restricted SQL FILE and settlements normal.
17:00 CI release and encrypted 17:00 archive ingress successful; no attacker SSH seen.
